name: Round the World Poker
description: Round the World Poker is a poker variant in which the required hand to win changes each deal: the first deal is won by high card, the second by pair, then two pair, three of a kind, and so on up through royal flush. Each deal is played like five-card draw with betting; only the hand type that wins the pot changes round by round.

overview.description: Round the World Poker is a poker variant in which the required hand to win changes each deal: the first deal is won by high card, the second by pair, then two pair, three of a kind, and so on up through royal flush. Each deal is played like five-card draw with betting; only the hand type that wins the pot changes round by round.

history.origins: Round the World is a home-game poker variant in which the winning hand type rotates each deal, from high card through royal flush. It is commonly played as part of Dealer's Choice and is documented in poker variant collections.
timeline: Early 20th century: Appears in home poker circles as a rotating-hand variant.
Present: Played in Dealer's Choice and mixed poker sessions.
history.cultural: Reflects American home-game culture of varying rules per round.
history.evolution: Replaced fixed hand-ranking with a cycle of required hand types per deal.

setup.players: Two to eight players; best with about six.
setup.dealing: Each deal: five cards face down to each player. The required hand to win that deal is determined by the round number (e.g. round 1 high card, round 2 pair, up to royal flush), then play follows standard five-card draw with a betting round, draw, and final betting round before showdown.

rules.objective: Win the pot by having the best hand that meets the current round's required hand type (e.g. this deal only a pair or better wins; next deal only two pair or better), or by forcing all others to fold.
rules.gameplay: 1. Agree the order of hand types (e.g. high card, pair, two pair, three of a kind, straight, flush, full house, four of a kind, straight flush, royal flush). 2. Each deal: dealer gives five cards face down to each player. 3. First betting round. 4. Draw: each player may discard and replace zero to three cards (or four if holding an ace). 5. Second betting round. 6. Showdown: remaining players reveal; the best hand that qualifies for this round's required type wins the pot. 7. Next deal uses the next hand type in the cycle.
keyRules: Only hands that meet the round's required type can win; a higher hand that does not qualify loses to a qualifying lower hand.
Standard five-card draw rules apply within each deal.
The cycle of hand types repeats after the final type (e.g. after royal flush, back to high card).

strategy.basic: Know the required hand type for the current deal; fold early if you cannot make that type after the draw.
strategy.intermediate: Track which hand types have been played; in later rounds (e.g. full house or better) bet aggressively when you qualify and others may not.
strategy.advanced: Use position and bet sizing to represent qualification in rounds where few players can make the hand.
tips: In high-card-only rounds, any pair is worthless; in pair rounds, two pair or better still wins.
Adjust draw strategy to the round: draw for the minimum qualifying hand when the pot is large.

variations.name: Short cycle
variations.description: Use fewer hand types per cycle (e.g. high card, pair, two pair, three of a kind, straight) then repeat.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Short cycle has no engine overrides; add overrides when implementing.

synthesis.shortDescription: Poker variant where the required hand to win rotates each deal from high card through royal flush; each deal is five-card draw with betting.
